business.title: Annual inflation up to 3.8% in the euro area
business.description: Overview The euro area annual inflation rate was 3.8% in September 2026, up from 3.2% in August. A year earlier, the rate was 2.2%. European Union annual inflation was 3.8% in September 2026, up from 3.2% in August. A year earlier, the rate was 2.6%. These figures are published by Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union. The lowest annual rates were registered in Sweden (1.0%), Hungary and Denmark (both 2.1%). The highest annual rates were recorded in Romania (6.5%), Lithuania (6.1%) and Bulgaria (5.6%). Compared with August 2026, annual inflation fell in one Member State, remained stable in three and rose in twenty-three. In September 2026, energy (+1.71 percentage points, pp), services (+1.52 percentage points, pp), non-energy industrial goods (+0.29 percentage points, pp) and food, alcohol & tobacco (+0.25 percentage points, pp) contributed positively to the annual euro area inflation rate. The euro area flash estimate for September 2026, published on 2 October 2026, was 3.8%. The next flash estimate of euro area inflation with data for October 2026 is scheduled for 4 November 2026. Methods and definitions Annual inflation is the price change of consumer goods and services between the current month and the same month of the previous year. Monthly inflation is the price change between the current month and the previous month. A contribution shows how much of the annual inflation rate comes from a particular component of the HICP. The contributions are calculated according to a method which ensures their additivity (allowing for rounding). Geographical information Up to December 31, 2025, the euro area included Belgium, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal, Slovenia, Slovakia and Finland (EA20). From 1 January 2026, the euro area also includes Bulgaria (EA21). The European Union includes Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Hungary, Malta, the Netherlands, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Finland and Sweden (EU27). The aggregate data series published in this Euro indicator release refer to the evolving composition of the euro area and the European Union. Thus, Euro indicator data for months up to December 2025 represent EA20 series, while Euro indicator data for January 2026 onwards represent EA21 series. Changes in the composition of the euro area are incorporated using a chain index formula. science.title: RNA sequencing significantly improves HYDIN diagnosis and defines the effects of common deletions in primary ciliary dyskinesia
science.description: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare genetic disorder affecting ~1:7500 individuals characterised by recurrent chronic respiratory infections, bronchiectasis, laterality defects, and infertility. While at least 60 PCD-causing genes are reported, approximately 30% of patients remain without a confirmed molecular diagnosis. PCD caused by biallelic HYDIN variants is difficult to diagnose due to a 98% homologous pseudogene (HYDIN2). Additionally, functional ciliary diagnostic testing can be inconclusive due to the lack of discernible HYDIN ciliary ultrastructure defects by electron microscopy. Our aim was to diagnose genetically unresolved PCD patients with strong clinical suspicion of HYDIN defects using RNA sequencing (RNA-seq). RNA-seq was performed on total RNA extracted from patients’ nasal epithelium cultured for 21 days at the air-liquid interface. Splicing abnormalities were detected using rMATS and genome-aligned reads were manually inspected using Integrative Genome Viewer. Thirteen individuals had strong clinical suspicion of PCD, normal TEM and inconclusive genetics: 11/13 had a single pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in HYDIN, 1/13 had no variants, and 1/13 required clarification of variant origin (HYDIN vs HYDIN2). RNA-seq resolved 11/13 (85%) of cases. The same complex pathogenic aberrant splicing events were seen in seven unrelated patients. This abnormal splice pattern was caused by a large 10-kilobase deletion spanning intron 17 to intron 18. RNA-seq increases the diagnostic yield for patients with suspected PCD and has exposed a HYDIN ‘hotspot’ variant, increasing the observed prevalence of HYDIN-related cases within our genetically diagnosed cohort. Routine PCD genomics testing will now incorporate investigation of this genetic region of HYDIN.

science.title: Disturbance resilient fuzzy variable gain super twisting sliding mode control for underactuated Furuta pendulum systems
science.description: The Furuta pendulum, also known as a rotary inverted pendulum, is a representative underactuated nonlinear system widely used for evaluating advanced control strategies. Its inherent instability, nonlinear dynamic coupling, and limited actuation make accurate stabilization particularly challenging, especially in the presence of model uncertainties and external disturbances. Conventional controllers, such as PID and fixed gain sliding mode controllers, may suffer from limited robustness, excessive control activity, or chattering when subjected to system uncertainties and disturbances. To address these limitations, this study proposes a disturbance resilient fuzzy Logic Based variable gain super twisting sliding mode controller (FLBVGSTA) for the stabilization of an underactuated Furuta pendulum. A state based sliding surface is formulated using the rotary-arm and pendulum states, while a fuzzy inference mechanism dynamically adjusts the super twisting gains according to the magnitude of the sliding variable. The nonlinear dynamics of the Furuta pendulum are derived using the Euler Lagrange formulation, and the finite time stability of the closed-loop system is investigated using Lyapunov based analysis under bounded disturbances. The proposed controller is evaluated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations and compared with FBSTSA and PID-STA controllers under identical simulation conditions. The results show that the proposed FLBVGSTA reduces the pendulum-angle RMSE by 5.0% compared with FBSTSA and by 78.05% compared with PID-STA. For the rotary-arm angle, the RMSE is reduced by 85.0% compared with FBSTSA and by 64.8% compared with PID-STA. In addition, the convergence time is reduced by 87.21% and 86.35% compared with FBSTSA and PID-STA, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed fuzzy variable gain super twisting strategy provides improved stabilization accuracy, faster convergence, and enhanced disturbance rejection while reducing unnecessary control activity.
